title: Towards Generating Contracts for Scientific Data Analysis Workflows
problem: Scientific data analysis workflows require manually specified contracts to verify execution expectations and correctness, but this labor-intensive manual specification hampers adoption in practice. Developers must discretionally specify suitable contracts without tool support.
motivation: Automatic contract generation enables contract-driven design adoption in scientific workflows by reducing the manual burden on developers while maintaining verifiable guarantees for dependability and portability.
method: An LLM-powered pipeline automatically generates code contracts from logical workflow descriptions. The approach is instantiated within Nextflow and evaluated on real-world Nextflow modules, using the LLM to infer contracts that encode task environment requirements and correctness properties.
key_novelty: Using Large Language Models to automatically synthesize verifiable code contracts from workflow descriptions, eliminating manual contract specification.
contributions: LLM-powered pipeline for automatic contract generation from workflow logical descriptions
Instantiation and evaluation within Nextflow workflow system on real-world modules
Demonstration that automatic generation produces substantial contracts as developer starting points
Framework enabling practical adoption of contract-driven workflow design
limitations: Limitations not discussed; work-in-progress with preliminary feasibility evaluation lacking comprehensive validation of contract correctness or completeness.
primary_theme: automatic contract generation for scientific workflows
